beforeafter.title: Before and
beforeafter.subtitle: Three real processes from companies I worked with. On the left, how it was done by hand. On the right, how it runs now.
beforeafter.leads_before: Every WhatsApp lead was copied into the CRM by hand, one at a time, and classified by whoever happened to be free.
beforeafter.leads_after: The message arrives, the data is extracted and validated, the CRM and PostgreSQL sync, and the right salesperson gets pinged.
beforeafter.reporting_before: Reports were assembled by hand from sales, inventory and CRM in separate systems. Nobody entirely trusted the numbers.
beforeafter.reporting_after: One warehouse with proper dimensional modelling, validation rules, and Power BI dashboards on verified data.
beforeafter.loads_before: Data loads ran sequentially and took hours to finish, with no way to tell whether something had failed.
beforeafter.loads_after: Parallelised Airflow pipelines with automated validation and alerts when something breaks.

story.title: The short version
story.p1: I started out writing web applications for small businesses in Santa Cruz. What ended up interesting me was not the screens but what happened behind them: people copying data between systems, reports that did not reconcile, hours lost to work a machine could do.
story.p2: So I moved toward data and automation. I built ETL pipelines processing millions of records a day, a corporate data warehouse with proper dimensional modelling, and workflows connecting WhatsApp, CRMs and databases in real time. The part I care about is the measurable part: 50% faster loads, 40% less time per lead, 95% report reliability.
story.p3: I work with clients in Bolivia and the United States, in English and Spanish. Lately I spend a lot of time wiring LLMs into real business processes, which is where I think most of the interesting work is right now.
story.p4: Outside client work I build my own products: software for people in Santa Cruz who solve things with a paper notebook today.
